content.text:
Double-check done — it turned up three real problems, all now fixed. Final state: 29 tests pass, `sun.py` 498 lines, `test_sun.py` 391, nothing committed.

## What the re-check found

1. **Squash was wrongly skipped on human overlays.** Driving `sun hook` as a real subprocess (JSON on stdin, the way Claude Code calls it) showed a turn where a human touched `h.txt` during the agent's `Write` never got squashed. My guard treated the human event sharing the agent's commit as "foreign". Fixed: squash proceeds when every commit in range is one of this agent's tool-call commits; overlay events get re-recorded against the turn commit (`overlay_of: <op id>`) so `sun log` still shows `[agent… turn1] [human:emma]` on the turn. Only standalone foreign commits (human sync between calls, another agent, manual `git commit`) block the squash.

2. **Claim-key mismatch leaked claims.** I had keyed in-flight claims by `sid/tool_use_id` (so parallel subagents sharing a `session_id` don't clobber each other), but if the id is only present in `PostToolUse`, the `PreToolUse` claim was never popped — the file stayed excluded from every future commit. Fixed with a fallback to the id-less claim; test asserts `active.json` is empty afterwards.

3. **`PostToolUse` without a `PreToolUse`** (hooks installed mid-session) attributed an Edit to the human. Now the payload's own file counts as claimed.

Also verified: per-call commits survive `git gc --prune=now` via `refs/sun/ops/*`; the installed hooks have no matcher (so Bash edits are captured as `hook_diff`); `demo_fresh.py` runs cleanly and `demo_sundial.py` still parses and uses only surviving helpers (`tool_file`, `char_edits`, `EDIT_TOOLS`).

Two things I could not verify here and you should watch on a real session:
- That your Claude Code version sends `tool_use_id` in hook payloads (if not, `tool_call_id` is `null`; attribution is unaffected).
- Repos that ran the old `sun init` keep the old `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` entries with an `Edit|Write|…` matcher; `install_hooks` sees `sun hook` already present and won't widen them, so Bash-made edits in those repos will still be synced as human until the matcher is removed by hand.
